title: Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program Final Rule (CMS-4215-F)
date_evidence: Fact Sheets Nov 05, 2026 Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program Final Rule (CMS-4215-F)
key_claim: On 5 November 2026 CMS issued the codifying final rule for the Negotiation Program from price applicability year 2029 and said final guidance on manufacturer effectuation of the maximum fair price in 2028, including for Part B drugs, is still to come in fall 2026, with 2029 effectuation policies to be codified in rulemaking in 2027.
frame_summary: CMS presents the final rule as codifying the programme for 2029 onward while leaving 2028 effectuation, including for Part B drugs, to guidance not yet issued.
verbatim_quote: CMS intends to release final guidance in fall 2026 to implement policies related to manufacturer effectuation of the MFP in 2028 for the Negotiation Program, consistent with the program instruction directive in sections 11001(c) and 11002(c) of the IRA. This guidance will specify the requirements for effectuation of the MFP, including with respect to drugs payable under Part B. CMS intends to codify MFP effectuation policies for 2029 and future years through Negotiation Program rulemaking in calendar year 2027.
verbatim_list: The final rule is effective Dec. 5, 2026.
notes: Confirmed on the live CMS page 08/11/2026; whitespace normalised.

title: Manufacturer Effectuation of MFP Draft Guidance for 2028 Medicare Drug Price Negotiation
date_evidence: Fact Sheets Jul 16, 2026 Manufacturer Effectuation of MFP Draft Guidance for 2028 Medicare Drug Price Negotiation
key_claim: CMS's 16 July 2026 draft guidance describes for the first time how manufacturers must provide the maximum fair price for Part B drugs from 2028, either by pricing at acquisition at or below the price or by a refund within 14 days, with four options for the standardized metric that sizes the refund, and recognises that a reliable actual acquisition cost is hard to establish.
frame_summary: CMS proposes a two-route delivery of the Part B price and opens the refund metric to comment because actual acquisition cost cannot be reliably measured claim by claim.
verbatim_quote: CMS recognizes that Primary Manufacturers and Part B providers may face significant challenges establishing a reliable actual acquisition cost for a selected drug that could be used to determine the MFP refund amount.
verbatim_list: CMS intends to require the same 14-day time frame for selected drugs payable under Part B as for selected drugs covered under Part D.
CMS intends to begin onboarding Primary Manufacturers with selected drugs for initial price applicability year 2028 by May 1, 2027.
Comments received by 11:59 PM Pacific Time (PT) on September 18, 2026 will be considered.
CMS is not, currently, assuming responsibility for nonduplication of discounts between the 340B ceiling price and MFP.
notes: Structural anchor (3-6 month band): the canonical CMS statement of the Part B delivery options. Confirmed on the live CMS page 08/11/2026.

title: MFPs beyond Part D: What Maximum Fair Prices mean for Part B stakeholders
date_evidence: WHITE PAPER MFPs beyond Part D: What Maximum Fair Prices mean for Part B stakeholders By Michelle (Klein) Robb, Victoria Robinson, and Katherine Holcomb 7 October 2026
key_claim: Milliman's actuaries show that the choice of refund metric changes provider margin on Part B drugs; an ASP-based refund erodes as the maximum fair price enters ASP, which could turn provider margin negative, and CMS will not publish ASP for negotiated drugs.
frame_summary: Milliman argues that effectuation, not the negotiated price, will decide who gains or loses on Part B drugs, because the refund metric and the ASP feedback loop are unresolved.
verbatim_quote: MFP is included in the calculation of ASP, which means ASP will fall over time as MFP is incorporated into the average. This will likely result in ASP diverging from true average acquisition costs and could cause the provider margin to become negative for selected drugs.
verbatim_list: Providers are reimbursed for Part B drugs at ASP plus a 6% add-on before sequestration.
an illustrative drug with a WAC of $12,000, an ASP (prior to MDPNP) of $10,000 (i.e., assuming a 20% supplier concession), and an MFP of $6,000
MFPs reflect average list price discounts of approximately 60% for IPAYs 2026 and 2027, based on discounts published by CMS.
The IPAY 2028 drugs primarily covered under the Part B benefit include Botox, Cimzia, Entyvio, Orencia, and Xolair.
CMS has indicated that it will not publish the ASP for negotiated drugs, making it challenging to use as a calculation metric.
Many commercial contracts are set at a percentage of the Medicare reimbursement rate or of ASP itself.
Once a drug has been selected, the MFP is effective until a generic or biosimilar alternative for that product has been marketed for at least nine months.
notes: Actuarial white paper. The $4,000 and $2,000 refund gaps in the figure are the analyst's arithmetic on Milliman's illustrative $12,000 / $10,000 / $6,000 case, assuming purchase at ASP as Milliman does.

title: Comments to CMS on Draft Guidance, Manufacturer Effectuation of the Maximum Fair Price in 2028
date_evidence: Comments for the Record September 18, 2026 Comments to CMS on Draft Guidance, Manufacturer Effectuation of the Maximum Fair Price in 2028 Michael Baker
key_claim: A market-oriented think-tank asks CMS to identify Part B claims through existing billing codes because all selected 2028 Part B drugs are biologics with their own codes, to size refunds on average sales price, and to publish a quarterly refund file so providers can estimate refunds.
frame_summary: AAF accepts the Part B delivery design but asks CMS to use existing billing infrastructure and a predictable, published ASP-based refund so that effectuation adds little cost of its own.
verbatim_quote: CMS notes that all selected drugs payable under Part B for 2028 are biologic products already assigned unique HCPCS codes containing only NDCs associated with the selected drug.
verbatim_list: CMS should also finalize its proposed public SDRA file and require its update quarterly in line with the existing ASP cycle.
notes: Comment letter to CMS from a think-tank that opposes government price setting but asks for low-burden implementation; read as a counter-position.

title: Third Medicare Drug Negotiation Cycle Closes, Including Part B Doctor-Office Drugs for the First Time
date_evidence: <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-11-01">; visible: By the Goodsurance editorial team November 1, 2026
key_claim: The third negotiation cycle closed on 1 November 2026, all 15 manufacturers signed agreements, and CMS must publish any agreed prices by 30 November 2026, the first-ever negotiated prices for drugs given in doctors' offices.
frame_summary: Goodsurance reports the close of the third cycle as a milestone for Part B drugs and sets 30 November as the next dated step.
verbatim_quote: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services now has until November 30 to publish any maximum fair prices that were agreed upon with drug manufacturers.
verbatim_list: All 15 manufacturers signed agreements to participate.
If finalized, those prices take effect January 1, 2028.
notes: Consumer-insurance news aggregator summarising CMS; used only for dates and counts, which are also CMS-stated.

title: Medicare Sent Its Final Drug Price Offers by September 30. Manufacturers Now Have Until October 31 to Respond.
date_evidence: <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-01">; visible: By the Goodsurance editorial team October 1, 2026
key_claim: CMS sent final price offers on all 15 third-cycle drugs by the 30 September 2026 deadline, and manufacturers had until 31 October 2026 to accept or reject them.
frame_summary: Goodsurance reports the statutory offer and response steps that closed the third negotiation cycle.
verbatim_quote: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services met the statutory September 30, 2026, deadline to send final maximum fair price written offers to the manufacturers of all 15 drugs selected for the third cycle of Medicare drug price negotiations.
verbatim_list: Each manufacturer must now accept or reject the offer in writing by October 31, 2026.

title: NICA Comments on CMS Draft Guidance Regarding Manufacturer Effectuation of the Maximum Fair Price in 2028
key_claim: The trade body for community infusion centres says the Part B refund process could create cash-flow and administrative burdens for independent practices, citing CMS's own acknowledgement, and that most members would need at least 3-6 months to prepare.
frame_summary: NICA argues that moving the Part B discount into a post-purchase refund loads cash-flow and administrative risk onto independent infusion providers.
verbatim_quote: In fact, CMS’s own draft guidance acknowledges that “independent physician clinics” are among the Part B providers likely to face material cash-flow problems tied to MFP effectuation.
verbatim_list: When surveyed, the majority of NICA members stated they would require a minimum of 3-6 months to operationally prepare for significant changes to the buy and bill ecosystem.
notes: Tier 4 advocacy body for community infusion providers; used as directional corroboration of the provider-side concern only.
